transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: OK, hey team, thanks for joining, uh, 15:00 on the dot. We got about 45 minutes. The goal is messaging refresh and demo prat\u2014 practice, sorry. Quick round robin intros?
[00:12] Carlos Mendez: Carlos here, SE, I'll run through the demo bits and re-record the clips we talked about.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Priya, content, I'll own the battlecards and one-pager.
[00:22] Tom Weller: Tom, Sales Ops, I'll make sure CRM playbook is updated.
[00:27] Lena Park: Cool. Start with messaging\u2014one line to customers, what's new. We want to be crisp: developer-first platform for predictable inference cost and latency, right?
[00:37] Carlos Mendez: Yeah, emphasize unified runtime — hosted, dedicated, private — same API. Customers care about predictable per token unit economics more than raw model ownership.
[00:47] Priya Singh: Maybe lead with the thesis: winners focus on serving. Quick line: "Ship LLM features quickly and keep unit economics predictable with Redwood."
[00:56] Tom Weller: Also call out SLAs for Dedicated and Private — enterprise hooks.
[01:02] Lena Park: Good. Now competitors — how do we frame OpenAI?
[01:08] Carlos Mendez: OpenAI is strong on model quality and ecosystem. Angle: if they want simplicity and earliest time to market, OpenAI is obvious. Our angle is production economics — predictable latency, cost controls, and private deployments.
[01:20] Priya Singh: For Anthropic, call out safety and policy play. We can say: Anthropic focuses on safety and aligned models; we focus on serving and operational guarantees. Don't say 'worse' or 'better' — just different priorities.
[01:35] Lena Park: Bedrock?
[01:38] Tom Weller: Bedrock is broad cloud integration, but operational complexity often higher — customers end up building their own orchestration. We can position Redwood as turnkey inference runtime with opinions.
[01:49] Carlos Mendez: Note: Replicate and smaller inference vendors are easy to use for prototyping, but they don't give you the batching, KV cache, or quantization toolkit we do. So we should always bring up caching + batching as cost levers.
[02:03] Lena Park: OK, messaging bullets seem clear. Now demo flow — we have 8 minutes total demo. Start with a product problem, then live query, then metrics slide, then architecture and rollout.
[02:14] Carlos Mendez: I propose: 1) Quick customer story (30s), 2) Live generation (2m), 3) Latency & cost slide (1m), 4) Deep dive on Dedicated vs Hosted (2m), 5) FAQ fallback & bundling (1.5m).
[02:29] Priya Singh: Make sure we call out smart routing and automatic fallback — customers like graceful degradation.
[02:35] Carlos Mendez: Agreed. Also show a short video clip of peak-latency under load — currently the clip says "Redwood Dedicate" in the subtitle, fix that.
[02:45] Lena Park: Haha yes, fix the subtitle. Also we want to rehearse responses to 'latency vs cost' question. Let's roleplay. 
[02:51] Tom Weller: Who wants to play buyer?
[02:53] Carlos Mendez: I'll play buyer. Lena, you go SE.
[02:56] Lena Park: Alright. (roleplay) Buyer: "We're seeing variable latency, can you promise p95 under 200ms?"
[03:06] Carlos Mendez (as buyer): Yeah, we have a SL\u2014 SLA requirement for p95.
[03:09] Lena Park (as SE): Great question; we typically qualify sequence length and throughput. For many apps we hit p95 under 200ms on dedicated pools; on hosted we recommend pinned capacity or smaller model variants to meet that SLO. We also use KV caching and batching to reduce per-token compute.
[03:28] Carlos Mendez (as buyer): And cost?
[03:30] Lena Park (as SE): Cost is a function of model choice and batching; we show customers how to run a pilot and analyze token-level breakdown in Redwood Console. We also recommend quantization profiles for background tasks.
[03:43] Carlos Mendez: Good. Pause — that last line about quantization might confuse sales — Priya, can you add a one-liner explaining quantization benefit?
[03:50] Priya Singh: Sure. Draft: "Quantization reduces model memory footprint and token compute, lowering costs by X-40% depending on model and workload." (note: X placeholder to be replaced after benchmarks)
[03:59] Lena Park: Don't put a hard percent until we have numbers. Say "materially lower" until Carlos records bench.
[04:05] Carlos Mendez: Right. I'll run updated bench and share numbers. I'll also capture a 2-minute clip showing live demo under 50 RPS to show batching effect.
[04:15] Tom Weller: For the demo script, remember to call out routing policies: region/cost/latency and automatic fallback to smaller variant if capacity is saturated. That's a big differentiator.
[04:28] Lena Park: Ok let's practice the pitch for that — 30 seconds. Start.
[04:30] Priya Singh: "Redwood routes inference requests by policy — you can route for lowest latency, lowest cost, or region. If a preferred variant is unavailable, automatic fallback keeps your app online with a compatible model variant."
[04:45] Carlos Mendez: Might be worth mentioning KV cache in the same breath: "Plus, prefix and KV caching reduce repeated token compute for chatty sessions."
[04:54] Lena Park: Nice. Now objections: customers will push on security and data residency. How do we answer private deployments?
[04:59] Carlos Mendez: Highlight Private deployment: VPC, on-prem option, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SOC 2. Simple bullet: "Same API, private control plane, customer-managed keys."
[05:12] Priya Singh: Add that Private is licensed with enterprise support and different billing model.
[05:16] Tom Weller: Also map out timeline: pilot -> Dedicated -> Private, often 3-6 months depending on compliance.
[05:23] Lena Park: Let's do a quick roleplay where buyer pushes on "we already use OpenAI". Carlos as buyer again.
[05:29] Carlos Mendez (as buyer): "We're on OpenAI, why would we move?"
[05:32] Lena Park (as SE): "OpenAI is great for model innovation; Redwood complements it — we make serving predictable and economical at scale. For example, if you need on-prem or VPC with KMS, or a predictable p95 for SLAs, Redwood is the serving layer you add."
[05:47] Carlos Mendez (as buyer): "What about model updates and regressions?"
[05:50] Lena Park (as SE): "We version models and have rollout policies with canary/A-B and automatic fallback. Also Redwood Optimize suggests quant and model profiles and quality-monitoring to detect regressions tied to prompt sets."
[06:05] Priya Singh: Ok good. Now specific demo practice — Carlos to run through live demo. We'll time it and provide feedback.
[06:12] Carlos Mendez: Starting demo run — opening slide, 30-second customer problem. (demo audio) "Our customer had 20% drop in conversions when latency spiked; Redwood helped stabilize p95 and reduce token cost."
[06:33] Carlos Mendez: Live generation — prompt: "Summarize user feedback and suggest 3 root causes." (typing sounds)
[06:45] [00:07] Carlos Mendez: Generated: "1) Model drift due to prompt changes; 2) High sequence lengths from debug data; 3) Misrouted requests causing cold starts."
[06:55] Lena Park: Nice. One nit: when you run the live generation, slow down and call out what you're typing; audience wonders about prompt engineering.
[07:03] Carlos Mendez: Noted. Also I should show the same prompt hitting dedicated pool vs hosted to show latency difference.
[07:08] Tom Weller: Good. After the live demo, show console token-level cost and per-route latency chart.
[07:15] Priya Singh: On the slide deck, can we add a small "how we measure" snippet — p50/p95/p99 definitions and measurement windows?
[07:22] Lena Park: Yes, add that to Appendix. 
[07:25] Carlos Mendez: A few transcription quirks I've seen in previous calls: the auto-subtitles keep calling it "Red wood" or "Redwood Dedicate". Priya, can you standardize brand spellings in the deck?
[07:36] Priya Singh: Will do, I'll run a find/replace and check the video subtitles.
[07:40] Lena Park: OK next, competitive objection: cost — show concrete pilot pricing. We should avoid public pricing in the deck but have a pilot template. Tom, you own that.
[07:50] Tom Weller: I'll add pilot pricing ranges and decision criteria to the CRM playbook.
[07:54] Lena Park: Roleplay again for security: buyer asks about audit logs and KMS.
[07:58] Carlos Mendez (as buyer): "Can you show logs and prove we can revoke keys?"
[08:02] Lena Park (as SE): "Yes — Private and Dedicated have audit logging and KMS/HSM integration; we can show an architecture diagram and runbook during an eval. We'll also provide SOC 2 docs on request."
[08:14] Carlos Mendez: Good. Priya, add a short slide with 'compliance artifacts' and a checklist.
[08:19] Priya Singh: On it.
[08:21] Lena Park: We're about 20 minutes in. Quick recap of feedback for Carlos's demo: slower narration, call out prompt engineering, show dedicated vs hosted comparison live, include console token breakdown, fix subtitles.
[08:34] Carlos Mendez: I'll make those edits and re-record the clip.
[08:37] Lena Park: For messaging, Priya — prioritize the one-pager: thesis + three differentiators + one-liner for each competitor.
[08:45] Priya Singh: Got it. Draft will include: "Why Redwood?" bullets: unified inference, cost controls, enterprise-grade deployments.
[08:54] Tom Weller: I'll prepare a short playbook snippet for qualifying pilots — success criteria like throughput, p95 target, data residency, and integration milestones.
[09:03] Lena Park: Planning next session: roleplay with external reps and timed demo. Schedule for next Tuesday 16:00 UTC. Tom to send calendar invite.
[09:12] Tom Weller: Will do.
[09:13] Lena Park: Anything else? Questions?
[09:17] Carlos Mendez: One minor competitor note — Anthropic has a safety angle that sometimes trumps ops; for customers focused on safety we should not push them away but position Redwood as complement.
[09:28] Priya Singh: Also capture a short rebuttal for "we already have on-prem infra" — highlight that Redwood reduces forklift work with a private control plane.
[09:36] Lena Park: Great. Closing notes: I'll send the updated checklist and schedule the follow-up roleplay. Thanks team.
[09:42] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional auto-caption errors e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated", some speaker labels merged in export. Keep these for authenticity.
